label: prop:meridian-holonomy-boost
title: Meridian holonomy is a boost: $\mathrm{barEven}(q)^2 - \mathrm{barOdd}(q)^2 = 4$
html:
Proposition. Meridian holonomy is a boost: \mathrm{barEven}(q)^2 - \mathrm{barOdd}(q)^2 = 4

The meridian holonomy of the cusp torus is multiplication by the substrate parameter q: one meridian turn is one application of the R-matrix — one crossing, one knot operation. Under the bar-split of the cusp shape, this holonomy satisfies the boost identity

  \mathrm{barEven}(q)^2 - \mathrm{barOdd}(q)^2 = 4 \qquad (q \neq 0),

the \cosh^2 - \sinh^2 = 1 relation (\times 4): the holonomy lies on a hyperbola, so one meridian turn is a hyperbolic rotation, not a compact spin.

Moreover, composing turns multiplies the holonomies q \mapsto q\,q', and this adds rapidity: the bar-parity shapes obey the addition laws

  2\,\mathrm{barEven}(q\,q') = \mathrm{barEven}(q)\,\mathrm{barEven}(q') + \mathrm{barOdd}(q)\,\mathrm{barOdd}(q'),
  2\,\mathrm{barOdd}(q\,q') = \mathrm{barOdd}(q)\,\mathrm{barEven}(q') + \mathrm{barEven}(q)\,\mathrm{barOdd}(q').

Additive rapidity corresponds to multiplicative holonomy — the boost group law. All three identities are formalized sorry-free over a generic field: holonomy_hyperbola, barEven_mul, barOdd_mul. At a real substrate q_0 > 1 the turn is a genuine boost of rapidity \ln q_0; only at a root of unity (\lvert q \rvert = 1) is it a compact U(1) spin.
